user_input: Create a omikuji game in ruby!
model_output:
An omikuji is a Japanese fortune-telling paper, often featuring a cute illustration and a prophetic message. Here's a simple game you can create in Ruby using a random number generator and if-else statements:

1. Create a new file called `omikuji.rb` and add the following code:
```ruby
puts "Welcome to the Omikuji game!"

def get_fortune
  # Generate a random number between 1 and 10
  fortune = rand(10)

  # Determine the fortunes based on the random number
  if fortune == 1
    puts "You got a great fortune! Congratulations!"
  elsif fortune == 2
    puts "You got a good fortune. Keep up the good work!"
  elsif fortune == 3
    puts "You got a neutral fortune. Keep it up, but don't get too excited."
  elsif fortune == 4
    puts "You got a bad fortune. You may want to reconsider some of your actions."
  elsif fortune == 5
    puts "You got a very bad fortune. Be careful, things may not go as planned."
  elsif fortune == 6
    puts "You got a terrible fortune. Watch out, things could get ugly."
  elsif fortune == 7
    puts "You got a horrible fortune. Stay out of trouble, things are not looking good."
  elsif fortune == 8
    puts "You got a catastrophic fortune. Don't even think about it, this is not a good idea."
  elsif fortune == 9
    puts "You got a disastrous fortune. Abort mission, turn back now."
  elsif fortune == 10
    puts "You got the worst fortune. Congratulations, you're screwed."
  end
end

get_fortune
```
2. Run the Ruby file by typing `ruby omikuji.rb` in your terminal or command prompt.
3. A random fortune will be generated and displayed in your terminal or command prompt.

Note: This is just a simple example to give you an idea of how to create a game in Ruby. You can expand on this concept and make the game more complex and interesting.
